name: The Memory Tithe City
summary: Veyr is a canal city where written memory is taxed, audited, and quietly weaponized.
premises: Written records hold political power because memory magic can verify ink but not speech.
The city survives on canal tolls, archive fees, and controlled access to old legal proof.
rules: Stamped ledgers can be authenticated with brine glass and are accepted as legal truth.
Any archive moved across district lines must be declared and taxed.
Bureaucratic magic leaves physical residue that skilled inspectors can notice.
taboos: Destroying a public ledger is treated as civic murder.
Using memory magic without a guild seal can trigger seizure of property and notes.
glossary: Memory tithe: the tax levied on recorded private knowledge.
Brine glass: treated glass used to verify lawful ink and seals.
